cards: Ridgely Whiteman, aged 19, discovers the Clovis site at Blackwater Draw in eastern New Mexico
The Anzick-1 burial is found near Wilsall, Montana
Max Uhle notes the site of Caral, though he does not recognise its hills as pyramids
A paper in Science by Ruth Shady, Jonathan Haas and Winifred Creamer brings Caral to wide attention
The Sacred City of Caral-Supe is inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site
Siyaj K’ak', a war leader linked with Teotihuacan, arrives at Tikal and a new dynasty takes power
K’inich Janaab Pakal begins his 68-year reign at Palenque
Pedro de Alvarado conquers the K’iche' kingdom of the Guatemalan highlands
The Spanish take Nojpetén, capital of the Itza, the last independent Maya kingdom
The Coronado expedition storms the Zuni town of Hawikuh and reaches the Rio Grande pueblos
Juan de Oñate founds the Spanish colony of New Mexico
Stela 29 is raised at Tikal, the earliest known dated monument of the Maya lowlands
The Mexica found Tenochtitlan, by tradition where their god Huitzilopochtli had promised
The Great Temple of Tenochtitlan is rededicated with the sacrifice of many captives
The fall of Tenochtitlan to the Spanish and their allies ends the Aztec state religion
The friar Diego de Landa burns Maya books and images at Maní in Yucatán
The Spanish take Nojpetén, capital of the Itza, the last independent Maya kingdom
Stela C at Tres Zapotes, an Epi-Olmec monument, records one of the earliest Long Count dates
The first known colossal head comes to light at Tres Zapotes, described by José María Melgar y Serrano
Julio C. Tello begins work at the site and calls Chavín the mother culture of the Andes
A debris flow buries much of the site and the modern town under mud
Chavín de Huántar is inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site
Drone surveys reveal many geoglyphs in Palpa province, now assigned to the Paracas culture
Michimalonco attacks the new Spanish town of Santiago in the Destruction of Santiago
Mapuche led by Lautaro defeat the Spanish at the Battle of Tucapel, where Governor Pedro de Valdivia is killed
Warriors led by Pelantaro defeat the Spanish at the Battle of Curalaba, starting the uprising that destroys the Spanish cities south of the Biobío
The Parliament of Quillín frees Spanish captives under an agreement between Mapuche and Spanish
Chile’s Indigenous Law officially recognises the Mapuche people, their language Mapudungun and their culture
Ray Hively and Robert Horn publish their study of lunar sightlines at the Newark Earthworks
Christopher Turner shows that the Hopeton earthworks align with sunrises and moonrises
Siyaj K’ak’ arrives at Tikal, and a new king linked to Teotihuacan takes power
K’inich Yax K’uk’ Mo’ founds the royal dynasty of Copán
Stela 29 records one of the earliest Long Count dates in the Maya lowlands
Sihyaj K'ahk', linked with Teotihuacan, arrives and King Chak Tok Ich'aak I dies
Tikal suffers a 'star war' defeat recorded at Caracol, opening a long hiatus
Calakmul's Yuknoom Ch'een II drives King Nuun Ujol Chaak from Tikal
Jasaw Chan K'awiil I defeats Yich'aak K'ahk' of Calakmul
Stela 11, Tikal's last dated monument, is raised in the Great Plaza
Walter Alva excavates the intact tomb of the Lord of Sipán at Huaca Rajada
The Teotihuacan war leader Siyaj K'ahk' arrives at Waka' in January, ten days before reaching Tikal: La Entrada, the first recorded meeting of Teotihuacan and the Maya.
Stela 15, a text-only monument, is erected naming the kings back to the mid fourth century and recording Siyaj K'ahk's coming.
Stela 34 portrays Lady K'abel; her tomb, found in the main pyramid temple in 2012, held an alabaster jar naming Lady Water Lily Hand and Lady Snake Lord.
Calakmul's ruler Yuknoom Took' K'awiil, likely the brother of Lady T'abi, is defeated, captured and sacrificed in Tikal's central plaza.
Yik'in Chan K'awiil of Tikal defeats Waka', makes it a vassal and takes the image of its celestial serpent to Tikal, recorded on Temple IV.
The Mexica found Tenochtitlan, by tradition, on an island in Lake Texcoco
Malintzin, a Nahuatl-speaking woman, becomes the interpreter of Hernán Cortés
The College of Santa Cruz de Tlatelolco opens, teaching Latin, Spanish and Nahuatl to young Nahua nobles
Alonso de Molina publishes his great dictionary of Nahuatl and Spanish
A royal decree of Charles III calls for Spanish to replace the Indigenous languages of the empire
Mexico’s law on linguistic rights recognises Nahuatl and other Indigenous languages as national languages
Tiwanaku is inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List
The Inca ruler Pachacuti begins the expansion that makes Quechua the language of an empire, by tradition
Domingo de Santo Tomás publishes the first grammar and dictionary of Quechua
A catechism in Spanish, Quechua and Aymara becomes the first book printed in South America
Peru makes Quechua an official language
A doctoral thesis written entirely in Quechua is defended for the first time, at the University of San Marcos in Lima
Archaeologists announce an unlooted Wari mausoleum at El Castillo de Huarmey
De Soto’s army burns the town of Mabila after an ambush; thousands of its people die
Tisquesusa becomes zipa after Nemequene dies of a war wound
Quesada's expedition enters Muisca lands and seizes the zaque at Hunza
Santa Fe de Bogotá is founded on 6 August in the zipas' former lands
The zipa Sagipa dies after torture; Tunja is founded on 6 August
The last zaque, Aquiminzaque, is beheaded at Tunja
A gold votive raft is found in a cave at Pasca
Christopher Columbus lands in the Bahamas, on the island the Taíno called Guanahaní
On his second voyage Columbus begins to demand tribute in gold and cotton from the Taíno of Hispaniola
Caciques of Puerto Rico, among them Agüeybaná II, rise against the Spanish, while Antonio de Montesinos denounces the enslavement of the islanders
The cacique Hatuey, who had fled from Hispaniola to Cuba to unite its peoples, is burned at the stake
9,399 people in Puerto Rico identify as Taíno in the United States census
Chan Chan becomes a UNESCO World Heritage Site and is listed as in danger
A severe drought begins, lasting until about 1167
Martin Frobisher’s search for the Northwest Passage brings the first well-documented contact between Europeans and Inuit, and he takes three Inuit captive to England
In the High Arctic relocation the Canadian government moves 17 Inuit families from Inukjuak to Resolute and Grise Fiord
Inuit found the Inuit Tapirisat of Canada, today Inuit Tapiriit Kanatami
The James Bay and Northern Quebec Agreement settles the land claim of the Quebec Inuit, with autonomy in the new region of Nunavik
Nunavut is established as a territory of Canada under the Nunavut Land Claims Agreement of 1993
Colonel John MacRae Washington leads 400 soldiers into Navajo country and signs a treaty, and the Navajo peace leader Narbona is killed on the way to it
On General James H. Carleton’s orders Kit Carson’s troops sweep through Navajo land, killing people, destroying crops and dwellings, fouling wells and seizing livestock
The US Army forces around 9,000 Navajo men, women and children on the Long Walk of over 300 miles to internment at Bosque Redondo
The Treaty of Bosque Redondo lets the surviving Navajo return to a reservation on part of their former homeland
The federal government begins the Navajo Livestock Reduction, made mandatory in 1935
Navajo transmitting Marine Corps combat simulations in their own language prove faster than any cryptographic facility, and the Marines recruit code talkers
Cahokia Mounds becomes a UNESCO World Heritage Site
Columbus reaches the Caribbean and hears from the Taíno of Carib raids
English and French settlers massacre an estimated 2,000 Kalinago at Bloody Point on Saint Kitts
France and England make the Treaty of Saint Charles with the Kalinago, leaving them Dominica and Saint Vincent as reserves
Britain has annexed Saint Lucia, Tobago, Dominica and Saint Vincent
After the Second Carib War the British expel the Garifuna of Saint Vincent to Honduras
The British government grants the Kalinago a territory of 3,700 acres on the east coast of Dominica
Dominica officially changes the people’s name from Carib to Kalinago
The Cocom of Sotuta massacre Xiu pilgrims at Otzmal
The Spanish found Mérida, and the Xiu lord of Maní makes peace with them
King Zuangua dies, probably of smallpox, and Tangaxuan II succeeds him
Cristóbal de Olid enters Tzintzuntzan and Tangaxuan II submits to Spain
Nuño de Guzmán has Tangaxuan II executed on 14 February
Vasco de Quiroga is appointed the first bishop of Michoacán
Itzcoatl's coalition defeats Azcapotzalco and the Triple Alliance is formed
The Purépecha rout Axayacatl's army, fixing the empire's western frontier
Ahuitzotl rededicates the enlarged Templo Mayor
Moctezuma II comes to power and centralises tribute and appointments
Hernán Cortés enters Tenochtitlan as Moctezuma II's guest
Spanish flee Tenochtitlan on La Noche Triste; smallpox then ravages the city
Tenochtitlan falls after a three-month siege; Cuauhtémoc is captured
Traditional date for the foundation of Tlaxcala by Teochichimec migrants
Tlaxcala fights Hernán Cortés, then allies with him on 23 September
The Spaniards shelter in Tlaxcala after La Noche Triste and the Battle of Otumba
Tlaxcalan forces help take Tenochtitlan, which falls on 13 August
Atahualpa defeats Huáscar, then is captured by Francisco Pizarro at Cajamarca
Atahualpa is executed and the Spaniards enter Cusco
Haudenosaunee war parties destroy the towns of the Huron Confederacy
The Covenant Chain alliance is agreed with the English at Albany
The Great Peace of Montreal ends decades of war with New France
The Grand Council covers its fire as the nations take sides in the American Revolution
Joseph Brant leads loyalist Haudenosaunee to the Grand River in Ontario
On 22 April Pedro Álvares Cabral's fleet of 13 ships lands at what is now Porto Seguro and takes possession of the land in the name of Manuel I.
Tomé de Sousa arrives as first governor-general with the first Jesuits and founds the capital, Salvador, on All Saints Bay.
Estácio de Sá founds Rio de Janeiro in the war against France Antarctique; the last French settlers are expelled in 1567.
An army under Domingos Jorge Velho destroys the Quilombo dos Palmares and kills Zumbi.
The capital of the State of Brazil moves from Salvador to Rio de Janeiro, nearer the gold of Minas Gerais.
Prince Regent John and the Portuguese court arrive in Brazil, fleeing Napoleon, and open its ports to friendly nations.
Tenochtitlan falls to Hernán Cortés and his indigenous allies
Antonio de Mendoza becomes the first viceroy of New Spain
The Manila galleon route links Acapulco with the Philippines
The Jesuits are expelled during the Bourbon reforms
Miguel Hidalgo launches the war of independence at Dolores
The Plan of Iguala and the Treaty of Córdoba end Spanish rule
Jacques Cartier claims the Gaspé Peninsula for France
Louis XIV makes New France a royal province
La Salle reaches the mouth of the Mississippi and claims Louisiana
The Great Peace of Montreal ends war with the Iroquois Confederacy
Quebec falls after the Battle of the Plains of Abraham
The Treaty of Paris cedes Canada to Britain
Manco Inca rebels and besieges Spanish-held Cusco for some ten months
Manco repulses the Spaniards at Ollantaytambo, then withdraws to Vitcos and Vilcabamba
Gonzalo Pizarro invades Vilcabamba; Manco escapes but Cura Ocllo is captured
Manco Inca is murdered at Vitcos by Spanish fugitives he had sheltered
Sayri Túpac renounces his claims in Lima and settles at Yucay
Titu Cusi Yupanqui accepts the Treaty of Acobamba
Titu Cusi dictates his account of the conquest for Philip II of Spain
Spanish forces take Vilcabamba; Túpac Amaru is captured and executed in Cusco
The New Laws of Charles V create the Viceroyalty of Peru
Silver is discovered at the Cerro Rico of Potosí
The University of San Marcos is founded in Lima
Túpac Amaru, last ruler of the Neo-Inca State, is executed in Cuzco
An earthquake and tsunami destroy much of Lima and the port of Callao
Upper Peru and Potosí pass to the new Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata
The rebellion of Túpac Amaru II begins in the southern Andes
Sucre defeats the royalists at the Battle of Ayacucho
Spanish Jesuits found the Ajacán mission, destroyed by local people the next year
The English found Jamestown; John Smith is brought before Wahunsenacah
Pocahontas marries John Rolfe, ending the First Anglo-Powhatan War
Opechancanough’s coordinated attacks kill some 347 colonists
Opechancanough is captured; the Treaty of 1646 makes the Powhatan tributaries
Cockacoeske signs the Treaty of Middle Plantation
The Lewis and Clark Expedition meets the Sicangu near the mouth of the Bad River, and a standoff ends when Black Buffalo grants the Americans passage
The Fort Laramie Treaty recognises Lakota title to nearly 100,000 square miles north of the North Platte in return for roads and military posts
General William S. Harney’s troops attack a Lakota and Cheyenne village at Blue Water Creek, killing at least 86 and taking 70 women and children captive
Custer’s expedition confirms gold in the Black Hills, and prospectors flood in against the terms of the 1868 treaty
Lakota and Cheyenne forces under Crazy Horse and Sitting Bull defeat Custer at the Battle of the Little Bighorn
Sitting Bull is killed at Standing Rock, and two weeks later the 7th Cavalry kills at least 270 Lakota in the Wounded Knee Massacre
In United States v. Sioux Nation of Indians the Supreme Court awards $122 million for the Black Hills, which the tribes refuse
Henry Hudson, hired by the Dutch East India Company, sails the Halve Maen into Upper New York Bay and up the river that bears his name as far as the site of Troy.
On 17 March the States General grants an exclusive trade patent between the 40th and 45th parallels; traders of the New Netherland Company build Fort Nassau near Albany.
On 3 June the Dutch Republic charters the Dutch West India Company with exclusive rights in West Africa and the Americas.
New Netherland becomes a province; 30 families land at Fort Orange and Noten Eylant from the ship Nieu Nederlandt under Cornelius Jacobsen May, the first director.
On 24 May Peter Minuit and Walloon colonists acquire Manhattan for goods worth 60 guilders and build Fort Amsterdam at its southern tip.
The Charter of Freedoms and Exemptions creates the patroonships; Rensselaerswyck becomes the only truly successful one.
Director-general Peter Stuyvesant conquers New Sweden on the Delaware; Jews are granted full residency in New Amsterdam.
On 27 August four English frigates under Richard Nicolls demand the surrender of New Amsterdam, which falls without resistance.
Louis XIV officially recognises French colonisation of Hispaniola and Tortuga, with slavery-based plantation agriculture and cattle farming.
The Code Noir regulates slavery and grants freed people full citizenship; the colony's first sugar windmill is built.
By the Peace of Ryswick Spain tacitly recognises French control of Tortuga and the western third of Hispaniola.
Mackandal, the one-armed maroon leader who united the maroon bands and raided for six years, is captured after a plot to poison the planters' water and burned alive at Cap-Français.
Some 8,000 plantations worked by 406,000 to 465,000 enslaved people produce half the sugar and coffee consumed in Europe and the Americas.
After the Vodou ceremony at Bois Caïman the enslaved of the northern plain rise, killing 2,000 Creoles and burning 280 sugar plantations within two months.
Civil Commissioner Léger-Félicité Sonthonax abolishes slavery in the colony by emancipation proclamation; Toussaint Louverture joins the Republic.
On 18 November Dessalines's army defeats the French at the Battle of Vertières near Cap-Haïtien; the last French troops withdraw and Haiti declares independence in 1804.
A Zeeland fleet captures the English colony, confirmed as Dutch by the Treaty of Breda
The Society of Suriname takes over the colony
The colony makes peace with the Ndyuka maroons
Slavery is abolished on 1 July, now commemorated as Keti Koti
The first indentured labourers from British India arrive
Suriname becomes an autonomous country within the Kingdom of the Netherlands
Sergeants led by Desi Bouterse seize power in a coup
Spanish records first mention the Comanche, allied with the Utes, near Taos
Comanches and allies attack the Spanish mission of San Sabá in Texas
Juan Bautista de Anza’s expedition kills the war leader Cuerno Verde
Ecueracapa concludes peace with New Mexico under Governor Anza
Council House Fight in San Antonio; Buffalo Hump leads a great raid to the coast
The Medicine Lodge Treaty assigns a reservation in Indian Territory
Mackenzie’s troops destroy the Comanche horse herd in Palo Duro Canyon
Quanah Parker’s Kwahadi band surrenders at Fort Sill
The Declaration of Independence is adopted on 4 July
The Treaty of Paris recognises American independence
The Constitution takes effect and George Washington becomes president
The Louisiana Purchase roughly doubles the country’s area
The Civil War begins after eleven Southern states secede
Union victory and the Thirteenth Amendment end slavery
The United States emerges from the Second World War as a superpower
Apollo 11 lands the first astronauts on the Moon
The Constitution of the United States takes effect, turning a confederation into the first modern federation
After the Sonderbund War, Switzerland’s new constitution turns its confederacy into a federal state
Seceding southern states form the Confederate States of America, and the American Civil War begins
The British North America Act unites three colonies in the federal Dominion of Canada
The German Empire is founded as a federation of 25 states under the king of Prussia
After referendums in each colony, six Australian colonies federate as the Commonwealth of Australia
India’s constitution comes into force, making the country a “Union of States”
The Soviet Union, a federation of fifteen union republics, is dissolved
The Constitution of the United States takes effect and George Washington is inaugurated as the first president
In Marbury v. Madison the Supreme Court asserts its power to strike down acts of Congress
Mexico’s first federal constitution creates a presidency on the American model
Brazil’s monarchy falls and Deodoro da Fonseca becomes the first president of a presidential republic
The Twenty-second Amendment limits American presidents to two terms
Chile’s armed forces overthrow President Salvador Allende, ending four decades of constitutional rule
Richard Nixon resigns as Congress moves to impeach him over the Watergate scandal
After mass protests, South Korea adopts a constitution with direct presidential elections
The Chickamauga Cherokee make peace with the United States at Tellico Blockhouse
The first written Cherokee law creates the Lighthorse Guard
The Cherokee Nation adopts a written constitution
The Cherokee Phoenix appears at New Echota; John Ross is elected principal chief
Worcester v. Georgia rules that Georgia’s laws have no force in the Cherokee Nation
Forced removal on the Trail of Tears begins
An Act of Union reunites the Cherokee, with Tahlequah as capital
Oklahoma statehood ends the Nation’s self-government
Jacques I is assassinated and a republican constitution is adopted
Alexandre Pétion is elected president as Haiti splits between republic and north
Pétion aids Simón Bolívar and becomes president for life
Boyer reunites Haiti after Henri Christophe’s suicide
Haiti occupies Santo Domingo, ruling all of Hispaniola
France recognises Haiti in return for an indemnity of 150 million francs
The May Revolution: an Open Cabildo dismisses Viceroy Cisneros and the Primera Junta takes power in Buenos Aires in the name of the captive Ferdinand VII.
United Provinces of the Río de la Plata
On 20 June the First Upper Peru campaign ends in the Disaster of Huaqui; Paraguay has already repelled Belgrano and Montevideo's fleet has destroyed the Junta's squadron at San Nicolás.
United Provinces of the Río de la Plata
On 31 January the Assembly of the Year XIII opens, abolishing the Inquisition, noble ranks and Indigenous labour drafts and freeing the children of slaves.
United Provinces of the Río de la Plata
On 20 June after William Brown's victories at Martín García and Buceo, Montevideo surrenders and Alvear occupies the last royalist capital of the viceroyalty.
United Provinces of the Río de la Plata
On 9 July the Congress of Tucumán declares the United Provinces in South America independent of Ferdinand VII, his successors and metropole.
United Provinces of the Río de la Plata
On 5 April San Martín's United Army defeats the royalists at the Battle of Maipú, consolidating the independence of Chile.
United Provinces of the Río de la Plata
The federal armies of López and Ramírez rout Rondeau's Directorial troops at Cepeda; on 11 February the Congress dissolves and the national government ends.
United Provinces of the Río de la Plata
The Eastern Bank becomes independent as Uruguay after British intervention in the Cisplatine War; the Federal Pact of 1831 follows.
United Provinces of the Río de la Plata
Paraguay defeats Belgrano’s army and ends the Spanish governor’s authority
José Gaspar Rodríguez de Francia becomes supreme dictator
A congress formally declares Paraguay’s independence
Alfredo Stroessner seizes power and rules until 1989
The Itaipú dam, shared with Brazil, begins generating power
A democratic constitution makes Guaraní an official language
Independence is proclaimed and secured at the Battle of Maipú
A new constitution creates a strong presidential state
Victory at Yungay ends the Peru–Bolivian Confederation
The War of the Pacific begins against Peru and Bolivia
Congress defeats President Balmaceda in a civil war
Augusto Pinochet’s coup overthrows Salvador Allende on 11 September
Voters reject Pinochet in a plebiscite
Democracy returns under President Patricio Aylwin
Congress of Angostura proclaims the Republic of Colombia after the Battle of Boyacá
Congress of Cúcuta adopts a constitution; the Battle of Carabobo frees Venezuela
Sucre wins the Battle of Pichincha and Quito joins the republic
Colombian armies end Spanish rule in South America at Junín and Ayacucho
José Antonio Páez leads the Cosiata revolt in Venezuela
Bolívar assumes dictatorial powers and survives an assassination attempt
Venezuela and Ecuador secede; Bolívar dies near Santa Marta
The remaining provinces are reorganised as New Granada
José de San Martín proclaims Peruvian independence in Lima
Sucre defeats the last royalist field army at the Battle of Ayacucho
Ramón Castilla abolishes slavery and the Indian tribute
Peru enters the War of the Pacific against Chile
The Treaty of Ancón cedes Tarapacá to Chile
Juan Velasco Alvarado seizes power and begins radical reforms
Alberto Fujimori closes Congress; Abimael Guzmán is captured
Pedro Castillo is removed after trying to dissolve Congress
Prince Pedro proclaims independence at the Ipiranga and is acclaimed Emperor Pedro I
Pedro I abdicates in favour of his five-year-old son
Pedro II is declared of age at fourteen, ending the Regency
The Eusébio de Queirós Law effectively ends the transatlantic slave trade
Paraguayan War begins; Brazil will bear most of six years of fighting
The Law of the Free Womb is passed
Princess Isabel signs the Lei Áurea, abolishing slavery
Marshal Deodoro da Fonseca's coup ends the monarchy
Guatemala City signs an act of independence from Spain
The Central American provinces are annexed to the First Mexican Empire
A congress declares the United Provinces of Central America independent
A federal constitution is adopted and slavery is abolished
Francisco Morazán takes Guatemala City, ending the civil war
Rafael Carrera’s rebels enter Guatemala City; three states secede
Carrera defeats Morazán at Guatemala City
Morazán is executed in San José, Costa Rica
Upper Peru declares independence at Chuquisaca as the Republic of Bolívar
Andrés de Santa Cruz forms the Peru-Bolivian Confederation
Chile occupies Antofagasta, beginning the War of the Pacific
The Treaty of Petrópolis cedes Acre to Brazil
The Chaco War with Paraguay begins
The National Revolution brings universal suffrage and nationalises the mines
Evo Morales becomes Bolivia’s first indigenous president
A new constitution creates the Plurinational State of Bolivia
The Treaty of Montevideo, fostered by Britain through Viscount John Ponsonby, ends the Cisplatine War and creates Uruguay as an independent state.
On 18 July the first constitution is adopted; the country is officially the Oriental State of Uruguay.
The last Blanco rising ends at the Battle of Masoller with the death of Aparicio Saravia; President José Batlle y Ordóñez's reforms follow.
Gabriel Terra dissolves the General Assembly in a coup and governs by decree; a new constitution of 1934 strengthens the presidency.
At President Juan María Bordaberry's request the armed forces disband Parliament and establish a civilian-military regime.
Julio María Sanguinetti takes office after the elections of 1984, restoring democracy and full freedom of the press.
On 11 December Uruguay becomes the first country to fully legalise cannabis, after legalising abortion in 2012 and same-sex marriage in 2013.
A Quito assembly declares the Southern District of Gran Colombia independent
Gabriel García Moreno is assassinated in Quito
The Liberal Revolution brings Eloy Alfaro to power
The Rio Protocol assigns most of the disputed Amazon to Peru
Oil exports begin through the Trans-Ecuadorian pipeline
Ecuador replaces the sucre with the US dollar
Venezuela secedes from Gran Colombia and adopts its own constitution
Slavery is abolished under President José Gregorio Monagas
The Treaty of Coche ends the Federal War
The Barroso II blowout reveals the oil riches of Lake Maracaibo
Dictator Marcos Pérez Jiménez is overthrown; the Punto Fijo pact follows
The oil industry is nationalised and PDVSA is created
A new constitution creates the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela
On 2 October hostilities between Texian settlers and Mexican troops open at the Battle of Gonzales, the first engagement of the Texas Revolution.
On 2 March the Convention of 1836 proclaims the Texas Declaration of Independence; David G. Burnet becomes interim president.
On 21 April major fighting ends, and the Treaties of Velasco, signed by Santa Anna as a prisoner, secure Texas's independence, which the Mexican Congress refuses to recognise.
On 3 March President Andrew Jackson appoints Alcée La Branche chargé d'affaires, the United States officially recognising the republic.
President Mirabeau B. Lamar moves the capital to the new town of Austin; the Lone Star Flag is adopted and France recognises Texas on 25 September.
After 34 Comanche leaders are massacred at peace talks in San Antonio, Buffalo Hump leads the Great Raid of 1840 to the Gulf coast; the Comanches are caught at the Battle of Plum Creek.
On 11 September Adrián Woll's 1,400 Mexican troops capture San Antonio; Texans fight at the Battle of Salado Creek while 53 surrendered volunteers are massacred nearby.
On 29 December Texas is annexed and admitted as the 28th state of the United States; power passes from the republic on 19 February 1846.
Honduras declares its separation from the Federal Republic of Central America
Marco Aurelio Soto moves the capital from Comayagua to Tegucigalpa
Manuel Bonilla invades with mercenaries financed by Samuel Zemurray
Tiburcio Carías Andino begins sixteen years of rule
The great banana strike wins workers the right to organise
Honduras and El Salvador fight the Football War
The army removes President Manuel Zelaya in a coup
Nicaragua becomes the first state to leave the Federal Republic of Central America
Managua is chosen as a compromise capital between León and Granada
The American filibuster William Walker makes himself president
José Santos Zelaya incorporates the Mosquito Reserve
US Marines land, beginning an occupation that lasts until 1933
Augusto César Sandino is murdered on the orders of Anastasio Somoza García
The Sandinista revolution overthrows Anastasio Somoza Debayle
Violeta Barrios de Chamorro defeats Daniel Ortega, ending the Contra war
A constitution declares El Salvador a sovereign and independent state
Rafael Carrera takes San Salvador and overthrows Gerardo Barrios
The abolition of communal lands opens the way for coffee estates
The army crushes a peasant uprising in La Matanza
El Salvador and Honduras fight the Football War
Archbishop Óscar Romero is assassinated while saying mass
The Chapultepec Peace Accords end the civil war
El Salvador adopts the US dollar
Rafael Carrera proclaims the Republic of Guatemala
The Liberal Revolution overthrows the conservative regime
Justo Rufino Barrios is killed at Chalchuapa trying to reunite Central America
The October Revolution opens a decade of democratic reform
Jacobo Árbenz enacts the agrarian reform of Decree 900
A CIA-backed invasion forces Árbenz to resign
Efraín Ríos Montt intensifies the scorched-earth campaign in the highlands
Peace accords end thirty-six years of internal armed conflict
The Seneca Falls Convention in New York adopts the Declaration of Sentiments, which demands the vote for women
Wyoming Territory gives women the vote; the American movement splits into two rival national associations
New Zealand becomes the first self-governing country to give all adult women the vote in national elections
Emmeline Pankhurst founds the Women’s Social and Political Union in Manchester
Finland gives women both the vote and the right to stand for parliament, the first European country to do so
Britain gives the vote to women over 30 who meet a property qualification
The Nineteenth Amendment to the United States Constitution is ratified
Swiss men vote to give women the vote in federal elections
On 15 January Emperor Faustin Soulouque abdicates after General Fabre Geffrard's revolution and the republic is restored, with Geffrard as president.
After President Vilbrun Guillaume Sam's execution of 167 prisoners and his lynching, US Marines land at Port-au-Prince; the occupation lasts until 1934.
Dominican dictator Rafael Trujillo's army bludgeons and bayonets 20,000–30,000 Haitians on the border in the Parsley Massacre.
François 'Papa Doc' Duvalier is elected president; he rules by terror until his death in 1971 and is followed by his son until 1986.
Jean-Claude 'Baby Doc' Duvalier leaves the country under US pressure after nationwide demonstrations.
Operation Uphold Democracy: 20,000 US troops enter Haiti and Jean-Bertrand Aristide, overthrown by Raoul Cédras's coup of 1991, is restored.
On 12 January a magnitude-7.0 earthquake kills between 160,000 and 316,000 people and leaves up to 1.6 million homeless; a cholera outbreak from a UN base follows.
On 7 July President Jovenel Moïse is assassinated at his residence; the presidency has remained vacant and the state has since collapsed.
Bartolomé Mitre defeats the Confederation at Pavón, reuniting Buenos Aires and the provinces
Argentina joins Brazil and Uruguay in the war against Paraguay
Julio Argentino Roca leads the Conquest of the Desert
The Sáenz Peña Law introduces secret and compulsory male suffrage
General José Félix Uriburu overthrows Hipólito Yrigoyen in the first military coup
Argentina loses the Falklands War to Britain
Economic collapse ends in riots and a sovereign default
On 20 December South Carolina votes unanimously for secession after Abraham Lincoln's election; Mississippi, Florida, Alabama, Georgia, Louisiana and Texas follow by 1 February 1861.
On 8 February delegates at the Montgomery Convention form the Confederate States of America; Jefferson Davis is elected provisional president the next day.
On 12 April Confederate forces under Beauregard bombard and take Fort Sumter in Charleston harbor; Lincoln calls up 75,000 militia and Virginia, Arkansas, Tennessee and North Carolina secede.
Davis is inaugurated under the permanent constitution for a six-year term; the Permanent Congress has opened in Richmond on 18 February.
On 16 April the Confederate Congress imposes the first mass conscription on North American territory, making white men from 18 to 35 soldiers for three years.
Lee's invasion of Maryland is turned back at Antietam and Bragg's of Kentucky fails; Lincoln's preliminary Emancipation Proclamation ends British and French thoughts of recognition.
Vicksburg and Port Hudson fall, closing the Mississippi, and Lee's strike into Pennsylvania is repulsed at Gettysburg; the Confederacy withdraws into an interior defence.
On 9 April Richmond having fallen when Lee's lines broke at Petersburg, Lee surrenders at Appomattox Court House; Davis is captured on 10 May and the last land forces surrender by June.
The Charlottetown and Quebec conferences agree the terms of Confederation
The British North America Act creates the Dominion of Canada on 1 July
Canada acquires Rupert’s Land and creates the province of Manitoba
The Canadian Pacific Railway is completed and Louis Riel is executed
The Canadian Corps captures Vimy Ridge
The Statute of Westminster confirms Canada’s legislative independence
Newfoundland joins Canada as the tenth province
The Constitution Act patriates the constitution and adds the Charter of Rights and Freedoms
Maximilian is executed at Querétaro and Benito Juárez restores the republic
Porfirio Díaz seizes power under the Plan of Tuxtepec
Francisco I. Madero’s call to revolt begins the Mexican Revolution
The Constitution of 1917 is promulgated at Querétaro
Plutarco Elías Calles founds the National Revolutionary Party
Lázaro Cárdenas expropriates foreign oil companies
NAFTA comes into force and the Zapatistas rise in Chiapas
Vicente Fox’s election ends seven decades of PRI rule
The constitution of August 1886 creates the centralised Republic of Colombia
Panama secedes with United States support
The assassination of Jorge Eliécer Gaitán sets off the Bogotazo and deepens La Violencia
The National Front begins sixteen years of shared Liberal–Conservative rule
A new constitution replaces the charter of 1886
The government and the FARC sign a peace agreement
Gustavo Petro becomes Colombia’s first left-wing president
On 20 May Cuba gains formal independence as the Republic of Cuba, its constitution granting the United States the right to intervene under the Platt Amendment.
After a rigged election veterans rise in the August Revolution; President Tomás Estrada Palma resigns with his cabinet, and the United States occupies the island until 1909.
The Partido Independiente de Color's attempt to set up a separate Black republic in Oriente is crushed by the army under General Monteagudo with considerable bloodshed.
Sugar prices peak and crash in the Dance of the Millions, ruining the country financially and strengthening foreign investors.
A general strike, sugar workers' uprisings and an army revolt force Gerardo Machado into exile; in September the Sergeants' Revolt under Fulgencio Batista overthrows his successor.
The Treaty of Relations ends the Platt Amendment, binding Cuba to favour the American economy in return for a guaranteed 22 per cent of the U.S. sugar market.
A new constitution with the rights to labour and health care is adopted, and Batista is elected president.
Batista seizes power in a coup before the presidential election, suspends the 1940 constitution and revokes most political liberties.
Panama declares independence from Colombia and signs the Hay–Bunau-Varilla Treaty
The Panama Canal opens on 15 August
Flag riots in the Canal Zone leave more than 20 Panamanians dead
The National Guard overthrows Arnulfo Arias, beginning military rule
Omar Torrijos and Jimmy Carter sign the canal treaties
The United States invades and removes Manuel Noriega
Panama takes full control of the canal on 31 December
The expanded canal with larger locks opens
The Supreme Court rules segregated public schools unconstitutional in Brown v. Board of Education
Federal troops escort nine Black students into Central High School in Little Rock, Arkansas
The Birmingham campaign and the March on Washington, where King speaks of his dream
The Civil Rights Act outlaws segregation in public places and discrimination in employment
The Selma to Montgomery marches lead to the Voting Rights Act
Martin Luther King Jr. is assassinated in Memphis, and Congress passes the Fair Housing Act
